back: A word that shows the relationship of a noun or pronoun to another word, especially in time, place or movement.
notes: on Monday, under the tree, into the room, with my friend.

back: at + clock time (at 9 a.m.); on + day or date (on Friday, on 25 May); in + month, year, season, part of the day (in June, in 2010, in the morning).
notes: Exception: at night, at the weekend.

back: at a point (at the bus stop, at school); on a surface or line (on the table, on the Harare road); in an enclosed space or area (in the room, in Bulawayo).
since + starting point (since Tuesday); for + length of time (for three days); during + a period named by a noun (during the holiday).
notes: While is a conjunction: while we were sleeping.

back: interested in, good at, proud of, afraid of, keen on, similar to, different from, absent from, responsible for.
rely on, depend on, accuse someone of, apologise for, prevent from, succeed in, object to, insist on, congratulate on.
discuss (the plan), enter (the room), reach (Harare), go home, attend (a meeting), resemble (her mother).
notes: Not 'discuss about', 'enter into the room', 'reach at'.

back: A verb after a preposition takes the -ing form: interested in becoming, look forward to meeting, succeed in winning.
because of, on account of, owing to (reason); in spite of, despite (contrast); instead of; in front of; in case of; by means of.
notes: In spite of the rain (not 'in spite of it rained').
